content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: SLO breach detected — streaming p99 tail latency 2.4s (SLO 2.0s) in prod-us-west for model redwood/open-7b. Current impact: ~7.8% requests >SLO, streaming stalls reported. Auto-escalation: paging #eng-oncall. Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/alerts/1701240000 :rotating_light:

maya: I'm seeing the same on dashboards. p95 ~900ms, p99 ~2.4s. Affected routes: /v1/stream-chat and /v1/generate-stream. Looks correlated with KV cache pressure spikes starting ~T-25m.

devon: I'm on it — taking lead. @priya can you check customer-facing queues? aj, can you grab K8s pod counts for serving tier in us-west?

priya: Customer queues: 3 customers with elevated retry rates; one (acme-inc) has streaming timeouts in their browser (~10% of sessions). I've DM'd SEs to set expectations.

aj: k8s: serving-pool-us-west: 42 replicas running, CPU normal, GPU utilization steady. No recent deploys. Logs show repeated kv cache miss spikes and eviction events. I'll paste relevant lines:

```
2026-02-12T15:02:11Z WARN kv_cache: slab_eviction triggered slab_id=3 free=80MB->12MB
2026-02-12T15:02:13Z INFO prefill: started prefill job shard=12 size=8MB
2026-02-12T15:02:14Z WARN decoder: decode_latency p95=180ms p99=1.1s
2026-02-12T15:02:16Z WARN kv_cache: eviction pressure rising, fragmentation_ratio=0.78
```

devon: Those logs match. Hypothesis: slab fragmentation + aggressive prefill bursts are causing paging and CPU stalls on host, leading to streaming tail stalls. Prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill is writing many entries that cause fragmentation; decode path then has to page or rehydrate causing tail stalls.

maya: Any evidence of disk paging or OOM killer?

aj: No OOMs. dstat shows increased soft-irq and io-wait on a subset of hosts that correlate with the eviction spikes.

devon: Quick mitigation plan (live):
- 1) Throttle prefill workers for us-west to 25% using runtime flag (temporary)
- 2) Increase KV cache slab threshold for streaming lanes (move streaming lanes to reserved slab if possible)
- 3) Route small fraction (~5%) of traffic to fallback quantized model (lower memory footprint) to relieve pressure
- 4) If needed, scale up serving pool by +8 GPUs (auto scaling trigger)

priya: From support, customers prefer short degradation over repeated timeouts. Recommend throttle + routing first.

devon: Executing step 1 now: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags/prefill_throttle -d '{"region":"us-west","pct":25}'`

ops-bot: Flag update: prefill_throttle(us-west)=25% applied by devops. Propagation to all prefill workers ~30s.

devon: Applying routing tweak: updating routing policy to send 5% of /v1/stream-chat to model redwood/open-7b-quant-fallback us-west pool.

ops-bot: Routing rule update confirmed.

maya: Post-mitigation metrics after ~2m: p95 down from 900ms to 520ms, p99 down from 2.4s to 1.3s. Eviction events still present but reduced frequency. Streaming stalls count decreased 60%.

aj: dstat/host metrics: io-wait down, soft-irq normalized on previously noisy hosts.

devon: Good. Next steps (short term):
- Keep prefill throttle at 25% for 15-30m while we monitor
- Leave 5% routing to fallback for 1 hour and measure quality/regressions
- If stable, plan a controlled increase of reserved slab for streaming lanes to avoid prefill interference

sre-lead: For customer impact notes: 3 customers affected, partial to moderate, no data exfiltration, degraded streaming. SEs already notified. Please update status page with brief note: "Intermittent streaming delays in US-WEST; mitigations in progress."

priya: I'll post status page update and notify the 3 customers directly.

devon: Logging for follow-up investigation: capture heap/kv-slab histograms on impacted hosts, collect prefill job traces, and gather decode latencies for the affected time window. Running traces: `./tools/collect_prefill_trace --shard 12 --since 15m --out /tmp/trace-1701240000.zip`

aj: Trace collection started. ETA ~3m.

maya: Oncall handoff note: I'm going to sleep in 40m. @devon please prepare a brief handoff message for the next oncall with current mitigations and metrics.

devon: Will do. Current state at 1701240120: mitigations applied, p99 trending down (1.1s now), streaming stalls dropping. Prefill throttle & 5% routing remain. Collecting traces & slab histograms.

sre-lead: If p99 falls below 1.2s and stays stable for 20m, we can step down from full incident to monitoring. Keep me posted.

devon: Understood. If degradation recurs, next escalation is to increase fallback routing to 15% and/or spin up extra serving capacity.

maya: Handoff message for next oncall: "Inc:1701240000 — KV cache fragmentation + prefill bursts caused tail streaming stalls in us-west. Mitigations: prefill_throttle=25%, 5% routing to quant-fallback, monitoring. Customers: 3 affected, one (acme-inc) had ~10% timeouts. Traces and slab histograms collected to /artifacts/1701240000. If p99 >1.5s re-escalate to sre-lead and consider immediate scale-up or increase fallback to 15%."

priya: Posted status page update and notified impacted customers.

ops-bot: Trace upload complete: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/1701240000/trace-1701240000.zip

devon: Leaving this thread in monitoring state. I'll follow up with a short postmortem after traces analyzed. Reassigning incident to "monitoring" channel state.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: INVESTIGATING -> MONITORING at 1701240135.

maya: Thanks team. Good job moving quickly. :thumbsup:
